newsitem.title: USA: American Brands sees Q4 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: American Brands sees Q4 restructuring charge.

text.p: American Brands Inc said Thursday it will take about $80 million in restructuring charges in the fourth quarter from consolidating operations of its British-based Gallaher tobacco unit.
The unit will consolidate cigarette making at its factory at Lisnafillan, Northern Ireland, and close its factory in Manchester, England, over the next three to four years, the company said.
American Brands said the charges, which equal about $55 million after tax, will cover primarily employee termination benefits.
About 950 jobs will be cut, the company said, but these will be partially offset by the creation of about 300 new jobs in the Northern Ireland plant.

American Brands said the consolidation should produce substantial annual savings. The company expects its previously announced plans to spin off Gallaher to be completed in the second or third quarter of 1997.
It said it is reviewing other productivity-enhancing opportunities "that may well result in an additional restructuring charge prior to the spinoff."
The company said that excluding the $80 million restructuring charge, it still expects to achieve its previously-announced 1996 earnings per share growth target in the range of 10 percent.
American Brands shares gained 1/8 Thursday morning to 48-3/8.
